sections.html:
Madison is in the southern part of Madison County, about 13 miles north of Jackson, and belongs to the Jackson metro area. Ridgeland is its southern neighbor, and Gluckstadt lies roughly 5 miles north. Interstate 55 crosses town with exits at Madison Avenue (Exit 107) and Highway 463 (Exit 108), U.S. 51 passes through the older center, and the Natchez Trace Parkway hugs the eastern edge. Highway 463 is the main business corridor.

In 2020 the census found 27,747 residents, compared with 24,149 ten years earlier, spread over 9,989 households. Of 10,418 housing units, 4.1 percent stood empty, and 11.1 percent of rentals did. Newcomers mostly arrived after 1980, which means many houses here are younger than the Mississippi norm.

The city covers about 26.4 square miles, a little over 4 percent of it water. The east side drains toward the Ross Barnett Reservoir, the north toward Bear Creek and the west toward Limekiln Creek. A lot that backs onto a creek or drainage easement will get a close look from an inspector, so be ready to explain how water moves across yours.

The city applies the International Property Maintenance Code through a dedicated code compliance officer. The building department lists permits for new homes, additions, renovations, foundations, roofs, fences, pools, demolition and rental property. Gas and electric permits are issued when utilities have been off for more than six months, which affects any house that has sat vacant.

City code pages cover housing condition, litter, signs, overgrowth, nuisances and vehicles. One rule is specific: no inoperative or unlicensed vehicle may be parked or kept on a premises, and a vehicle in major disassembly must be inside an enclosed structure.

A municipal environmental court has heard code cases since January 2019. Ignoring a notice can mean a fine of up to $1,000 per day, plus up to 90 days in jail. Confirm current penalties with the city. The practical lesson for sellers is that an open violation on an inherited or vacant house only grows.

  • File the city's code violation form if you want to learn whether a complaint sits open against your address.
  • If a homeowners association exists, no permit is issued without its written approval, so contact the association early.
  • Keep copies of past permits for roofs, additions and pools.
  • If utilities have been off for months, plan on a permit before gas or electric comes back on.

Rules are on the City of Madison building and permits page.

Severe weather is the main physical risk to a Madison roof, and buyers know it. Expect questions about an old patch, a sagging ridge line or a past insurance claim, and dig out the paperwork before you list or accept an offer.

A skipped permit is the other common surprise. Roofs, foundation work, fences, pools and demolition all require one in Madison, and a gap shows up at inspection. An investor planning a renovation will normally discount for it rather than demand a fix. Neighborhood with an association? Ask for its resale documents early as well.

sections.h2: How property taxes work when you sell
sections.html:
The bill comes from Madison County in November or December and is payable by February 1 of the next year. Ownership is fixed as of each January 1, so the owner of record that day gets the bill. A February 1 that lands on a weekend or holiday rolls to Monday with no penalty. Inside city limits, three rates stack: county, school district and city.

Property classType of propertyAssessment ratio
ISingle-family, owner-occupied residential10%
IIOther real property, such as a rental house15%
IIIPersonal property, except motor vehicles15%
IVPublic utility property30%
VMotor vehicles30%

At closing, the agent usually apportions the current year between the two sides. A disputed valuation goes through the Madison County chancery clerk, who can set a Board of Supervisors hearing, generally before the first Monday in August.

The county tax collector is at 146 W. Center Street in Canton. Ask there for payoff figures on any back taxes before you close.

Under Section 89-1-503, most sellers owe the buyer a written property condition disclosure statement, handed over as soon as practicable before title moves. A buyer who gets the form after making an offer can walk away in writing: three days after hand delivery, five days after it is mailed.

Skipping the form does not make questions disappear, because the law presumes a buyer without a statement is on notice to ask. Even cash buyers who purchase as is want to hear about roofs, drainage, termites, flooding and earlier repairs, so honest written answers save time.

Homestead exemption timing matters too. Applications go to the county tax assessor from January 1 to April 1, and a new owner or new occupant may have to reapply. The chancery clerk must record the deed before January 7 for the exemption to count that year, so a late-year closing needs planning.

sections.h2: Listing, selling alone or selling for cash
sections.html:
• Listing: suits updated houses in popular neighborhoods and takes longer. It can bring the top price when you are willing to wait out showings, inspections and the lender's appraisal.
  • For sale by owner: no commission, but you carry the disclosure form, contract and negotiation.
  • Cash sale: fits inherited houses, tenant-occupied homes, code violations, worn-out roofs and short deadlines. Price gives a little in return for speed, fewer contingencies and no repair requests.

Madison is known for appearance standards, so a neglected house stands out to neighbors and code staff. That pushes many owners of vacant or inherited homes to sell rather than carry taxes, insurance and mowing. A tidy house in the right subdivision can still do well on the open market.

If you want a number without commitment, we can review the address and explain how a cash offer works. You owe nothing if you decline.

You can sell an inherited house as is, once you have legal authority to do so. Ask the chancery clerk or an attorney about estate paperwork before you take an offer. Then the steps are the usual ones: a contract, a title search for liens and back taxes, payoff of anything owed, and a deed signed at closing. Gather any past permits and repair receipts, since heirs often do not know the house's history. If the house has been empty, check the utilities and any code notices before you show it to anyone.

faqs.q: How far is Madison, MS from Jackson?
faqs.a: About 13 miles north. Interstate 55 connects the two, with Madison exits at Madison Avenue and Highway 463.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due on a house in Madison, MS?
faqs.a: By February 1 of the year following the January 1 assessment. When that date lands on a weekend or holiday, the following Monday is penalty-free. Bills are mailed in November or December.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace a roof in Madison?
faqs.a: Yes. Madison's building and permits department requires one for roofs, and for fences, foundation work, pools and demolition.

faqs.q: What happens if a Madison house has a code violation?
faqs.a: The code compliance officer notifies the owner and allows time to fix it. If the problem stays, the case can go to Madison's environmental court. Contact the city to confirm the current process and penalties.

faqs.q: Must I give a buyer a disclosure statement in Mississippi?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Section 89-1-503 sets the duty, with delivery due before title transfers. If the buyer receives it late, the buyer can withdraw within three days of in-person delivery or five of mailing.
